This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,

L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: KNI-272, a peptidomimetic with a tert-butyl amide, thioether, and hydroxyethylamine motif closely related to the query, had an absolute oral bioavailability of 36.4% after post-prandial oral capsule administration in patients, exceeding the 20% threshold.

Atazanavir, a peptidomimetic HIV protease inhibitor with tert-butyl and hydroxyethyl motifs, has oral bioavailability >90% when taken with food in humans, supporting high F for this structural class under fed conditions.

The query is a peptidomimetic with the same tert-butyl amide, hydroxyethyl, and thioether/aryl features and is assessed under a fed state; the physicochemical prior (high MW/logP, poor solubility) is not affirmative evidence of F<20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule itself.
KNI-272 evidence is based on n=2 patients; atazanavir bioavailability report type is unspecified.
Fed-state formulation and dose for the query are not specified; solubility/dissolution and first-pass metabolism are not experimentally characterized.
Structural similarity to KNI-272 and atazanavir is qualitative; no numeric similarity score is supplied.
